scope: Proposition 3.2 (Observation paths and cavities) of the manuscript “Cutoff throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase” (preprints/Cutoff-throughout-the-high-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-phase-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d99d391c8c3ed79f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed b, k, C, c, γ > 0 and events of disorder probability tending to one on which the following assertions hold, for the full model and for every model obtained by deleting one site. Along the observation experiment just defined, all posterior heat-bath gaps are at least γ, except on an ordinary observation event of probability at most Ce−cn. On the same good paths all posteriors satisfy Theorem 3.1 with the same constant. The exceptional event and a stopping time before loss of these properties can be chosen independently of any test function. The constants are common to all cavities.
